F001.acceptance: (1) When resolvable to a durable root, records carry canonical_repo {path_key, path_display, durable_checkout=true, origin_key?}, surviving compaction; when unresolvable from a temp path (C3 case 3b) the field is absent, never a temp canonical. (2) repo.path_key is unchanged and still drives bucket/conflict/locality logic, proven by a regression test (C2). (3) compact_ledger usage-count invariant, proven by a before/after fixture: in a fixture of duplicate records, legacy/no-field rows count as 1 and rows carrying observed_count sum correctly; compacted output preserves the same derive_buckets grouping plus the summed observed_count, and canonical_repo survives compaction; F003 reads the identical observed_count for a canonical repo before and after compaction (a before==after assertion, not merely 'a count test exists'). (4) Mixed-attribution compaction is fail-closed and tested: a bucket containing both canonical-bearing and legacy/non-canonical rows, or multiple canonical keys, emits canonical_compaction_conflict=true, omits canonical_repo, carries no canonical observed_count, and F003 ignores it so observed_count is neither inflated nor dropped silently. (5) durable_checkout describes the canonical repo; a temp worktree of a durable repo yields durable_checkout=true (C2/C3-3a), and a temp path is never self-canonicalized (C3). (6) No raw home path or raw origin URL is persisted anywhere (C1). (7) Records written before this feature still load; tests cover all three C3 cases, legacy-record, bucket-regression, compaction count invariance, mixed-attribution compaction conflict, C8 sidecar-lock acquisition on BOTH the append path and compact_ledger (concurrent-append serialization, plus a compaction-vs-append and compaction-vs-backfill race proving no lost write and no stale-inode rename), and no-secret-shape.

F002.acceptance: (1) The backfill engine consumes the F006 evidence contract and stamps canonical_repo onto matching historical records idempotently (re-run is a no-op), and any written path_display is the recomputed scrubbed display; literal evidence under the operator home is normalized to <home> and never copied through raw. (2) The deterministic C4 evidence matrix is implemented and tested: absent key, missing required field, wrong value type, raw-secret-shaped value, path_key mismatch, non-reconstructable scrub token, failed path-key confirmation, reconstructed temp canonical path, durable_checkout=true claimed for a temp canonical path, and durable_checkout=false claimed for a confirmed-durable canonical path are refused and reported, never guessed; durable_checkout written to the ledger is recomputed from the reconstructed canonical path, never trusted from evidence; origin_key is copied only from the single confirmed canonical evidence object after hash-shape/no-secret validation. (3) Backfill write mode runs inside the held C8 sidecar-lock context owned by the F005 entrypoint (F002 requires it and refuses direct write without it — no self-acquire); because both the live writer and the backfill acquire the sidecar lock BEFORE opening the ledger data file, no concurrent writer can hold a stale data-file inode across the rename; a concurrent append is serialized into the rewritten ledger or the backfill fails without replacement (exit 2), never lost. Evidence defects are split per C4 into file-fatal (exit 2, stamp nothing) vs per-record row-level skip+report (exit 0). (4) The evidence file is local-only and not committed, enforced by repo-local ignore plus commit-guard test/doc check. (5) The command field is never parsed (C6). (6) A fixture mirroring the 51 records collapses the three observed paths to one canonical repo key; ledger record order and unrelated fields are preserved.

F003.acceptance: (1) observed_canonical_from_ledger() is implemented and tested as the explicit ledger adapter: records without canonical_repo or with canonical_compaction_conflict=true are skipped, rows aggregate observed_count by canonical_repo.path_key with legacy/no-field rows counting as 1, scrubbed path_display is preserved, durable_checkout is carried, max last_seen is preserved, and record.command is never read. (2) registered_canonical_from_registry() is implemented and tested as the registry adapter: existing paths are canonicalized before pure reconcile; missing and unresolved paths emit canonical_repo_key=null, registry_path_key=sha256(normalized stored registry path)[:16], canonicalization_status, and scrubbed path_display; multiple active-eligible entries canonicalizing to one canonical_repo_key dedupe to a single row with the deterministic lexicographically-first registry_name winner, registry_conflict=true, and conflicting_registry_names; dedup considers ONLY active-eligible entries (eligibility determined before winner selection), so an inactive/path-missing/unresolved entry can never suppress an active entry for the same key regardless of name order. (3) reconcile() returns {used_unregistered, registered_active, registered_stale, registered_path_missing, registered_unresolved}; canonical rows are keyed on canonical_repo_key, registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved rows are keyed by registry_name + registry_path_key with canonical_repo_key=null; reconcile has no filesystem/git IO and zero-state yields empty arrays. (4) C5 defaults and registered-row truth table are pinned and tested: window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp=last_seen, inclusive observed_count >= min_count and last_seen >= now-window_days; missing path -> registered_path_missing; unresolved canonicalization -> registered_unresolved; inactive -> no active/stale row; existing canonicalized registered path with absent/invalid/stale/low-count observed row -> registered_stale; existing canonicalized registered path passing both thresholds -> registered_active; a registered row with no observed row for its canonical_repo_key emits observed_count=0 and last_seen=null, and the ledger adapter skips invalid timestamps rather than poisoning the aggregate. (5) Mixed-attribution compacted rows marked canonical_compaction_conflict do not inflate or drop canonical observed_count. (6) suggested_name derivation for used_unregistered rows is deterministic, project-name-regex safe, collision-safe with canonical_repo_key hash suffix, and JSON-safe. (7) Temp-prefix / non-durable usage never appears as used_unregistered (C3); isolated/D010-like fixtures produce used_unregistered vs registered_active; registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved key shapes are tested; adapters/reconcile never read command (C6).

F004.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic projects discover --json` serializes the F003 reconcile projection in the pinned field contract after building both observed_canonical and registered_canonical; default human output is concise; empty-state serializes to empty arrays without error. (2) The command supplies the C5 default values and configured CLI overrides to F003 reconcile inputs; F003 owns policy correctness and the active/stale truth-table tests. (3) JSON output contains canonical_repo_key + scrubbed display + counts/recency + suggestion_status + suggested_name only; no raw home path and no reconstructed add-command path appear in JSON (C1); registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved JSON rows carry canonical_repo_key=null plus registry_name and registry_path_key and NO observed_count/last_seen (those two null-keyed states have no canonical key to join observed usage to, matching the C5 narrowing), not a fake canonical key; registered_active/registered_stale rows carry registry_conflict + conflicting_registry_names and emit observed_count=0/last_seen=null when no observed row exists; the exact --json field names, value types, and suggestion_status enum (can_render_command|needs_manual_path) match the pinned field contract in this feature's description. (4) Default human output reconstructs the add-command path operator-locally using suggested_name and the three C1 path rules. (5) The CLI path never parses record.command (C6), never installs/modifies/removes/chains/reads/depends on git hooks (C7), and the isolated/D010-like fixtures produce used_unregistered vs registered_active respectively.

F005.acceptance: (1) The C4-pinned backfill entrypoint consumes default global-config evidence/ledger paths or explicit overrides, supports preview and write modes, reports with the stable schema, and follows the C4 status contract. (2) Write mode makes F005 the sole C8 sidecar-lock owner — it acquires the `<ledger>.lock` sidecar once (before opening the data file) and passes a held-lock context into F002 (which refuses direct write without it, never self-acquiring), holding it across the full critical section — and tests prove a concurrent append is serialized or the backfill refuses without replacing the ledger, with no double-acquire and no stale-inode rename loss. (3) Reported ledger/evidence paths are scrubbed. (4) Tests cover configured-home defaults, explicit path overrides, no-write preview behavior, single-lock-owner / no-double-acquire, status behavior, report schema, and the C7 negative hook guard.

F006.acceptance: (1) The C4 evidence contract is implemented and tested: required top-level keys, version 1.0, canonical repo map keyed by canonical path key, observation-key map with list values, only allowed canonical repo fields, required field presence, exact value types, and no-secret-shape validation before any field can be copied. (2) Malformed or ambiguous evidence is classified deterministically and split into file-fatal vs row-level (C4): file-fatal structural defects (not valid JSON/parse error, missing required top-level keys, wrong schema_version, top-level type error where canonical_repos or observation map is not a map) abort the whole run; row-level per-record defects (unknown canonical references, mismatched path keys, unknown fields, missing required fields, wrong value types, raw-secret-shaped values, non-list values, zero or multiple mappings for a record) are skip+report. (3) Optional origin and temp-observed fields are accepted only in the allowed canonical repo shape; origin_key must be hash-shaped and is rejected if it looks like a raw origin URL. F006 validates durable_checkout only as a boolean shape; its semantic truth is recomputed by F002 against the reconstructed canonical path.
